# USP é a latino-americana mais bem classificada no THE World Ranking – Jornal da USP

## USP é a latino-americana mais bem classificada no THE World Ranking

## Além da USP, a Unicamp e a Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Chile são as melhores universidades da América Latina

09/10/2025 - Publicado há 4 meses

## Texto: Erika Yamamoto

## Arte: Simone Gomes

![](https://jornal.usp.br/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20251009_ranking-2026.jpg)

Foto:[Times Higher Education – THE](https://sinter.ufsc.br/2025/10/09/resultado-da-ufsc-no-world-university-rankings-2026-da-times-higher-education/)

A USP é a melhor universidade latino-americana, de acordo com o THE World University Rankings, um dos principais rankings universitários internacionais. Elaborado pela consultoria britânica Times Higher Education (THE), o ranking foi divulgado hoje, dia 9 de outubro.

Classificada no grupo de 201-250, a USP se iguala a instituições como a Universidade de Illinois (Estados Unidos), Universidade de Surrey (Reino Unido), Universidade de Wollongong (Austrália), Universidade Tianjin (China) e Universidade de Tel Aviv (Israel).

No topo da lista está a Universidade de Oxford, seguida pelo Instituto de Tecnologia de Massachusetts (MIT, na sigla em inglês); Universidade Princeton e Universidade de Cambridge estão empatadas na terceira colocação. Das dez primeiras posições, sete são de instituições norte-americanas.

A USP melhorou em 9 dos 18 indicadores adotados pelo ranking: reputação acadêmica, número de doutores titulados, orçamento, relação doutorados/bacharelados, reputação em pesquisa, investimentos em pesquisa, número de estudantes estrangeiros, colaboração internacional e captação de recursos da indústria.

“Neste ano, o destaque positivo desse ranking fica para o eixo Ensino, em que melhoramos em 4 dos 5 indicadores e subimos da 78ª para a 68ª colocação global nessa dimensão. No eixo Ambiente de Pesquisa, estamos na 107ª posição global e no eixo Indústria, na 128ª colocação”, destaca a coordenadora do Escritório de Gestão de Indicadores de Desempenho Acadêmico (Egida), Fátima Nunes.

![](https://jornal.usp.br/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/20220628_fatima-300x300.jpg)

*Fátima Nunes - Foto: Arquivo Pessoal*

Ao todo, o Brasil tem 59 instituições classificadas. A Universidade Estadual de Campinas (Unicamp) é a segunda brasileira mais bem posicionada, no grupo entre 351-400. Em seguida, aparecem a Universidade Estadual Paulista (Unesp), a Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ) e a Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS), no grupo de 601-800.

Na edição deste ano, o ranking avaliou cerca de 2.100 instituições de ensino superior de 115 países. A avaliação levou em conta 18 indicadores, agrupados em cinco eixos: Ensino, Ambiente de Pesquisa, Qualidade da Pesquisa, Indústria e Internacionalização.

| THE World University Ranking 2025 | | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1º | University of Oxford | Reino Unido |
| 2º | Massachusetts Institute of Technology | Estados Unidos |
| =3º | Princeton University | Estados Unidos |

| 10º | Yale University | Estados Unidos |

| 351-400 | Universidade Estadual de Campinas (Unicamp) | Brasil |
| 401-500 | Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile (PUC-Chile) | Chile |

## Reconhecimento internacional

A USP também se destacou em outros rankings universitários internacionais divulgados neste ano. No QS World University, elaborado pela Quacquarelli Symonds (QS), a USP foi a universidade brasileira mais bem classificada, na 108ª posição. No QS Latin America & The Caribbean Ranking, a Universidade ficou na segunda posição.

No Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU), elaborado pela consultoria chinesa Shanghai Ranking Consultancy, a USP foi classificada no grupo entre a 101ª e a 150ª posição, sendo a universidade ibero-americana mais bem colocada.

Em outro ranking da consultoria Times Higher Education, o THE University Impact, a USP ficou na 101-200ª posição. O ranking avalia como as universidades do mundo todo estão contribuindo para os Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS) da Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU), em termos de pesquisa, divulgação e governança.

Mais informações sobre o ranking podem ser obtidas na página do **[Escritório de Gestão de Indicadores de Desempenho Acadêmico (Egida)](https://egida.usp.br/rankings/)** da USP.

Não consigo “confirmar na página/tabela oficial do **THE World University Rankings 2025**” as **posições/faixas** dessas universidades porque, ao acessar os perfis oficiais do THE (USP/Unicamp/UFRJ/Unesp/UFMG) e a página da tabela 2025, o conteúdo que aparece no scraping **não exibe o bloco de “Rankings / World University Rankings 2025”** (ele mostra principalmente “About…” e, no caso da tabela, só os destaques). Ou seja: **não dá para verificar e citar, com evidência direta do site oficial, as faixas 2025** para USP, Unicamp, UFRJ, Unesp, UFMG etc. com as ferramentas disponíveis aqui.

O que eu **consigo** trazer do domínio oficial do THE (mas **não é a tabela 2025 completa**) é esta página do THE Student “Study in Brazil”, que declara explicitamente as faixas globais (aparentemente do WUR 2025) para algumas universidades brasileiras:

Fonte (THE Student): https://www.timeshighereducation.com/student/where-to-study/study-in-brazil  
Trecho relevante (“Top universities in Brazil”):  
- **University of São Paulo (USP)**: **201–250**  
- **University of Campinas (Unicamp)**: **351–400**  
- **Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ)**: **601–800**

Com base **somente** nesse trecho (que não lista todas as que você pediu), dá para afirmar parcialmente o “top Brasil” no WUR 2025:
1) USP (201–250)  
2) Unicamp (351–400)  
3) UFRJ (601–800)  
(As posições 4 e 5 não aparecem nesse recorte.)

Para eu **confirmar o top 5 Brasil** e as faixas de **Unesp, UFMG** (e “outras”), preciso de uma destas opções:
- você me envia um **print** da tabela do THE WUR 2025 filtrada por Brazil (ou a lista), ou  
- você me passa o **link exato** da página do THE onde aparecem as linhas da tabela (com o filtro aplicado) / ou um link que contenha os resultados já listados, para eu extrair, ou  
- você autoriza que eu use uma **fonte espelho** (não-oficial) para pegar as faixas e depois eu tento corroborar com páginas institucionais/notícias (mas isso não seria “na página oficial/tabela oficial”).

Se você mandar o print/URL do ranking filtrado, eu retorno com:
- faixa global WUR 2025 de **USP, Unicamp, UFRJ, Unesp, UFMG,** etc.  
- **top 5 Brasil** confirmado (com evidência/link).

# University of São Paulo | World University Rankings

The University of São Paulo is a large Brazilian public university, and is considered one of country's more prestigious educational institutions.

Founded in 1934, the University of São Paulo came about through a collaboration of existing schools such as the Faculdade de Direito do Largo de São Francisco (Law), the Polytechnic School (Engineering) and the Escola Superior de Agricultura Luiz de Queiroz (Agriculture).

Now, the university has created new departments, and is one of the largest institutions of higher education in Latin America.

Four of its eleven campuses can be found in the city of São Paulo while the remaining campuses are in the cities of Bauru, Lorena, Piracicaba, Pirassununga, Ribeirão Preto and two in São Carlos.

The university has an remarkable 70 libraries installed across the various campuses for students to use and enjoy.

A significant proportion of scientific papers published by Brazilian researchers are produced at the University of São Paulo.

The university also houses five affiliated hospitals, 24 museums and galleries – with half a million visitors per year – two theatres, a cinema, and its own TV channel run by students.

However, the University of São Paulo have no accommodation within campus, or outside. The search for accommodation must be carried out by students in accordance to their economic conditions and interests.

Notable alumni include Antonio Candido de Mello e Souza, a Brazilian writer, professor, sociologist and literary critic, Brazilian lawyer and Vice President Michel Miguel Elias Temer Lulia, and Guido Mantega, Brazil's former Finance Minister.

# University of Campinas | World University Rankings

## About the University of Campinas

Basic information and contact details for the University of Campinas

![institution](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/academic-ui-assets/dsc/svg/flat/institution.svg?4)

Campinas is a city in the Sao Paulo state region, and is home to the main campus of the State University of Campinas (Unicamp).

The multi-discipline university also has affiliate campuses in Brazilian cities such as Limeira and Paulínia. Campinas is known not only for its temperate climate at the Tropic of Capricorn but also its wide range of cultural centres such as dozens of cinemas and bars, known locally as “barzinhos”.

The university was opened in 1966, and although one of Brazil’s younger institutions has established itself as a primary medical and scientific research centre. As part of this research and development the university produces a high amount of patented material, outstripping other larger institutions and companies. A major breakthrough was achieved in 2003 when scientists from Unicamp licensed a patent for genetic death detection, and in more recent years scientists at Unicamp have developed a test for detection of the Zika virus.

Also in Campinas and maintaining a strong working relationship with Unicamp is the National Synchrotron Light Laboratory. This institute is a benefit to students studying physics and nanotechnology, and is home to the only particle accelerator in South America. Outside of the sciences, students at Unicamp may take undergraduate courses in arts such as Dance and Communication Studies, or in humanities such as Business Administration and Social Sciences.

International undergraduates will need to sit an exam before acceptance, which will require a strong understanding of the Portuguese language. Like all state run universities, both Brazilian and international students do not pay tuition fees. The most common airport for international students to fly into is the Guarulhos International Airport, located around 135km from the Campinas campus.

Alumni of Unicamp include actor Petrônio Gontijo, historian and gay rights activist Luiz Mott, and economist Paulo Renato Souza.

# Federal University of Rio de Janeiro | World University Rankings

The Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, sometimes known as the "University of Brazil" and commonly abbreviated to UFRJ, is one of the largest and best known universities in Brazil. Founded by the Brazilian State in 1792, the university has gone on to have an enormous influence on public life in Rio, being responsible for laboratories, libraries and hospitals.

The University operates across a number of campuses and facilities throughout Rio de Janeiro, but is primarily focused on Ilha do Fundão, an artificial island off the western shore of Rio’s famous Guanabara Bay. This campus, known as College City, offers a huge range of services and activities for students including a free shuttle bus services for crossing Rio de Janeiro, various restaurants and cafes, a sports centre, as well as accommodation for students.

UFRJ can also lay claim to a number of high-quality academic facilities, such as the largest ocean tank in the world, as well as a domestically operated maglev train system.

As one might expect for a higher education institution of this size and reach, UFRJ offers a huge range and variety of undergraduate courses (more than 170), as well and numerous avenues for postgraduate and research students. UFRJ also distinguishes itself with a significant level of international co-operation, with extensive opportunities for foreign students to come and study in Rio.

The university can also boast of having produced a succession of successful alumni, including writer Jorge Amado, Nobel Peace Prize nominee Osvaldo Aranha, and physician Oswaldo Cruz.

# Universidade Estadual Paulista (Unesp) | World University Rankings

São Paulo State University (UNESP), founded in 1976, is one of Brazil’s largest public universities with 24 campuses throughout the State of São Paulo.

Its multi-campus model allows UNESP to offer a varied academic programme with diverse activities. As one of Brazil’s foremost research universities, it cites subject strengths in health, engineering, communications, humanities, arts, social sciences and theoretical sciences.

UNESP is international recognised for the quality of its research, teaching and its initiatives to promote cultural diversity in the classroom. Its ethos emphasises critical thinking, humanist principles, sustainability, technological innovation and democratic participation in equal measures.

The university’s various campuses are also home to a diverse range of contemporary artworks, historical artefacts, farms, museums and a zoo, as well as hospitals and libraries.

São Paulo is Brazil’s wealthiest and most populous State, vibrant and cosmopolitan. Its capital, the city of São Paulo, is the country’s financial and cultural centre, home to a host of iconic architecture and events such as the São Paulo Art Biennial and the Brazilian Grand Prix. The city also hosts the largest LGBT Pride Festival in the world.

# Federal University of Minas Gerais | World University Rankings

While the first higher learning education centre in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais was created in 1839, the modern day Federal University of Minas Gerais was founded in 1927. Upon its inception UMG combined a number of schools in the area in fields of law, medicine and engineering.

More recently established courses are agronomy, performing arts, computational mathematics, and automation.

UMG is located in the east Brazilian city of Belo Horizonte, a marvel of urban planning modelled around Washington D.C. The city also has a strong footballing culture, having been a host city in the 1950 and 2014 World Cups. A key conduit for travel in and out of the city is Confins International Airport, located on the city outskirts.

Sitting below the equator, the UMG holds its winter festival every July. The celebration brings together artists from across Brazil and the world to engage in courses, workshops and street exhibitions.

Every year there is also a "Knowledge Week" on campus, with the aim of sharing information and developments across different academic branches at the university. Graduates can also sign up to Academic Enrichment activities which can help them broaden their educational horizons outside a specialised area of study.

UMG also recognises the need for the university to communicate and foster the opportunities of students across economic and ethnic backgrounds, and is committed to this goal with scholarship programmes and outreach initiatives.

Notable alumni of UMG include former Brazilian prime minister Tancredo Neves, president Dilma Rousseff, and musician Samuel Rosa. Strong connections with former students are maintained through the Always UFMG Program.

# Study in Brazil

Perhaps best-known for its sport and breathtaking scenery, Brazil is home to more than 2,500 universities, with elite institutions including the University of São Paulo, the biggest public university in the country and one of the best in Latin America. Also home to São Paulo State University, Brazil’s largest city and financial capital is also considered the nation’s cultural centre, home to a plethora of museums, art galleries and concert halls - and it has a vibrant nightlife.

Brazil’s 8,000km of coastline include thousands of spectacular beaches. Also unmissable is carnival season, which starts in February. Rio de Janeiro’s carnival is the biggest in the world, with more than two million people lining the streets each day to witness more than 300 bands and samba schools.

Brazil produces a third of the world’s coffee and is renowned for a wide variety of street food. The country's football team has won the World Cup more than any other nation, and football, by far the most popular sport, has been likened to a religion in the country. # University of São Paulo | World University Rankings

The University of São Paulo is a large Brazilian public university, and is considered one of country's more prestigious educational institutions.

Founded in 1934, the University of São Paulo came about through a collaboration of existing schools such as the Faculdade de Direito do Largo de São Francisco (Law), the Polytechnic School (Engineering) and the Escola Superior de Agricultura Luiz de Queiroz (Agriculture).

Now, the university has created new departments, and is one of the largest institutions of higher education in Latin America.

Four of its eleven campuses can be found in the city of São Paulo while the remaining campuses are in the cities of Bauru, Lorena, Piracicaba, Pirassununga, Ribeirão Preto and two in São Carlos.

The university has an remarkable 70 libraries installed across the various campuses for students to use and enjoy.

A significant proportion of scientific papers published by Brazilian researchers are produced at the University of São Paulo.

The university also houses five affiliated hospitals, 24 museums and galleries – with half a million visitors per year – two theatres, a cinema, and its own TV channel run by students.

However, the University of São Paulo have no accommodation within campus, or outside. The search for accommodation must be carried out by students in accordance to their economic conditions and interests.

Notable alumni include Antonio Candido de Mello e Souza, a Brazilian writer, professor, sociologist and literary critic, Brazilian lawyer and Vice President Michel Miguel Elias Temer Lulia, and Guido Mantega, Brazil's former Finance Minister.

# University of Campinas | World University Rankings

## About the University of Campinas

Basic information and contact details for the University of Campinas

![institution](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/academic-ui-assets/dsc/svg/flat/institution.svg?4)

Campinas is a city in the Sao Paulo state region, and is home to the main campus of the State University of Campinas (Unicamp).

The multi-discipline university also has affiliate campuses in Brazilian cities such as Limeira and Paulínia. Campinas is known not only for its temperate climate at the Tropic of Capricorn but also its wide range of cultural centres such as dozens of cinemas and bars, known locally as “barzinhos”.

The university was opened in 1966, and although one of Brazil’s younger institutions has established itself as a primary medical and scientific research centre. As part of this research and development the university produces a high amount of patented material, outstripping other larger institutions and companies. A major breakthrough was achieved in 2003 when scientists from Unicamp licensed a patent for genetic death detection, and in more recent years scientists at Unicamp have developed a test for detection of the Zika virus.

Also in Campinas and maintaining a strong working relationship with Unicamp is the National Synchrotron Light Laboratory. This institute is a benefit to students studying physics and nanotechnology, and is home to the only particle accelerator in South America. Outside of the sciences, students at Unicamp may take undergraduate courses in arts such as Dance and Communication Studies, or in humanities such as Business Administration and Social Sciences.

International undergraduates will need to sit an exam before acceptance, which will require a strong understanding of the Portuguese language. Like all state run universities, both Brazilian and international students do not pay tuition fees. The most common airport for international students to fly into is the Guarulhos International Airport, located around 135km from the Campinas campus.

Alumni of Unicamp include actor Petrônio Gontijo, historian and gay rights activist Luiz Mott, and economist Paulo Renato Souza.

# University of Campinas | World University Rankings

## About the University of Campinas

Basic information and contact details for the University of Campinas

![institution](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/academic-ui-assets/dsc/svg/flat/institution.svg?4)

Campinas is a city in the Sao Paulo state region, and is home to the main campus of the State University of Campinas (Unicamp).

The multi-discipline university also has affiliate campuses in Brazilian cities such as Limeira and Paulínia. Campinas is known not only for its temperate climate at the Tropic of Capricorn but also its wide range of cultural centres such as dozens of cinemas and bars, known locally as “barzinhos”.

The university was opened in 1966, and although one of Brazil’s younger institutions has established itself as a primary medical and scientific research centre. As part of this research and development the university produces a high amount of patented material, outstripping other larger institutions and companies. A major breakthrough was achieved in 2003 when scientists from Unicamp licensed a patent for genetic death detection, and in more recent years scientists at Unicamp have developed a test for detection of the Zika virus.

Also in Campinas and maintaining a strong working relationship with Unicamp is the National Synchrotron Light Laboratory. This institute is a benefit to students studying physics and nanotechnology, and is home to the only particle accelerator in South America. Outside of the sciences, students at Unicamp may take undergraduate courses in arts such as Dance and Communication Studies, or in humanities such as Business Administration and Social Sciences.

International undergraduates will need to sit an exam before acceptance, which will require a strong understanding of the Portuguese language. Like all state run universities, both Brazilian and international students do not pay tuition fees. The most common airport for international students to fly into is the Guarulhos International Airport, located around 135km from the Campinas campus.

Alumni of Unicamp include actor Petrônio Gontijo, historian and gay rights activist Luiz Mott, and economist Paulo Renato Souza.

# Study in Brazil

Perhaps best-known for its sport and breathtaking scenery, Brazil is home to more than 2,500 universities, with elite institutions including the University of São Paulo, the biggest public university in the country and one of the best in Latin America. Also home to São Paulo State University, Brazil’s largest city and financial capital is also considered the nation’s cultural centre, home to a plethora of museums, art galleries and concert halls - and it has a vibrant nightlife.

Brazil’s 8,000km of coastline include thousands of spectacular beaches. Also unmissable is carnival season, which starts in February. Rio de Janeiro’s carnival is the biggest in the world, with more than two million people lining the streets each day to witness more than 300 bands and samba schools.

Brazil produces a third of the world’s coffee and is renowned for a wide variety of street food. The country's football team has won the World Cup more than any other nation, and football, by far the most popular sport, has been likened to a religion in the country. But many also like volleyball and, to a slightly lesser extent, mixed martial arts and basketball. Famous Brazilians include footballer Pelé and the late Formula 1 racing driver Ayrton Senna.

Public universities have free tuition for home and international students, but places are limited and most students attend private institutions.

# Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025

![Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025](https://images-intl.prod.aws.idp-connect.com/hca-cont/img/default/img_px.gif)

O aguardado *Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025* acaba de ser divulgado com as melhores universidades do mundo. Após analisar minuciosamente 2.092 instituições de 115 países e regiões, o ranking proporciona um panorama completo sobre o ensino superior global. Confira os destaques da nova edição!

## **Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025**

A [University of Oxford](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study-in-the-uk/applying-to-university/como-se-candidatar-a-oxford-no-reino-unido/) é a melhor universidade do mundo pelo nono ano consecutivo, de acordo com a Times Higher Education. Da mesma forma que no ano passado, todas as instituições nas dez primeiras posições são do Reino Unido e dos Estados Unidos. Não só isso, as universidades em questão também são exatamente as mesmas, algumas apenas trocaram de lugar. A [Princeton University](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study-in-usa/city-focus/como-estudar-na-universidade-de-princeton-estados-unidos/) subiu duas posições para o quarto lugar, enquanto a [Stanford University](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study-in-usa/city-focus/como-se-candidatar-a-stanford-university/) caiu quatro posições para o sexto.

Outros países começam a aparecer a partir do 11º lugar, ocupado pela [ETH Zurich da Suíça](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study-in-switzerland/city-focus/eth-zurique-na-suica/), seguida por duas universidades da China. A Tsinghua University e a University of Peking subiram uma posição em relação ao ano passado. A primeira, inclusive, liderou recentemente o [*Times Higher Education Asia University Rankings*](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study-in-china/city-focus/melhores-universidades-da-asia-2024/)das melhores universidades da Ásia.

### **As melhores universidades do mundo segundo Times Higher Education 2025**

1. University of Oxford, Reino Unido

2. Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), EUA

3. Harvard University, EUA

4. Princeton University, EUA

5. University of Cambridge, Reino Unido

6. Stanford University, EUA

7. California Institute of Technology, EUA

8. University of California, Berkeley, EUA

9. Imperial College London, Reino Unido

10. Yale University, EUA

[![Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025](https://images-intl.prod.aws.idp-connect.com/hca-cont/img/default/img_px.gif)](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study/international/schools-colleges-university/list.html) 

Como de costume, as [universidades dos Estados Unidos](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study/us-usa/international/schools-colleges-university/211/list.html) têm o melhor desempenho geral. A maioria das 30 melhores do mundo são estadunidenses, incluindo o segundo lugar, o [MIT](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study-in-usa/city-focus/por-que-o-mit-e-uma-das-melhores-universidades-do-mundo/), agora classificado como a melhor instituição na América, tomando a posição antes ocupada pela Stanford. O Reino Unido também continua bem com 12 instituições entre as 100 melhores.

A edição não foi muito positiva para as universidades da Austrália e Nova Zelândia. Dezessete das instituições australianas caíram na lista e apenas quatro subiram de posição, entre elas, a [UNSW Sydney](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study/australia/school-college-university/unsw-sydney-university-of-new-south-wales/72233/international.html) e a [Macquarie University](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study/australia/school-college-university/macquarie-university/72221/international.html). Nenhuma das oito universidades da Nova Zelândia melhorou sua posição em relação à edição 2024. No entanto, ambos os países mostram sua força geral, com um total combinado de 12 instituições dentro do top 250. A melhor de todas é a [University of Melbourne](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study/australia/school-college-university/the-university-of-melbourne/879/international.html), em 39º lugar.

Já a Ásia continua a progredir a cada edição. A região tem uma incomparável aparição de 853 universidades no *Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025* - 116 a mais do que no ano passado. Embora a maioria seja da China, incluindo sete no top 100, quase todo o continente conseguiu um lugar na lista. A Nanyang Technological University, de Singapura, por exemplo, subiu duas posições e ficou entre as 30 melhores do mundo, juntamente à sua conterrânea National University of Singapore, em 17a. E a japonesa University of Tokyo ficou em 28a.

Confira o top 30 do *Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025*:

11. ETH Zurich, Suíça

12. Tsinghua University

13. Peking University

16. Johns Hopkins University

17. National University of Singapore

=18. Columbia University

=18. University of California, Los Angeles

20. Cornell University

21. University of Toronto

=22. UCL (University College London)

=22. University of Michigan-Ann Arbor

24. Carnegie Mellon University

25. University of Washington

26. Technical University of Munich

27. Duke University

28. University of Tokyo

29. University of Edinburgh

30. Nanyang Technological University

### **USP fica entre as 200 melhores do mundo**

O Brasil é um dos três países que conseguiram um lugar entre as 200 melhores universidades do mundo em relação a 2024, com a Arábia Saudita e os Emirados Árabes Unidos, no *Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025*, "destacando a ascensão do ensino superior em mercados emergentes", segundo o site oficial do ranking.

A Universidade de São Paulo (USP) ficou na 199a posição, seu melhor desempenho desde 2013, graças, principalmente, à melhoria no indicativo relacionado à indústria (renda e patentes).

A Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio de Janeiro (PUC-Rio), a terceira instituição brasileira mais bem classificada, também melhorou sua posição, subindo da faixa 801-1.000 para 601-800 este ano. As outras três no top cinco do Brasil permaneceram nas mesmas faixas: a Universidade Estadual de Campinas (Unicamp) em 351-400; e a Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ) e a Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS), ambas em 601-800.

O Brasil agora tem 61 universidades classificadas no *Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025*, com cinco instituições a mais este ano. Em comparação ao resto da América do Sul, as universidades brasileiras têm a maior pontuação média nos pilares de ensino, ambiente de pesquisa e indústria.

#### **A metodologia do Times Higher Education World University Ranking**

O *Times Higher Education World University Ranking 2025* baseia-se no desempenho das universidades em cinco áreas diferentes - ensino, ambiente de pesquisa, qualidade da pesquisa, indústria e perspectiva internacional -, medidas e pontuadas de acordo com 18 indicadores de desempenho, todos com ponderação porcentual. Quando combinados, eles formam uma pontuação geral para cada universidade na lista.

**Ensino: 29,5%**

- Reputação do ensino: 15%

- Proporção entre funcionários e alunos: 4,5%

- Proporção de doutorado para bacharelado: 2%

- Proporção de professores com título de doutor: 5,5%

- Renda institucional: 2,5%

**Ambiente de pesquisa: 29%**

- Reputação da pesquisa: 18%

- Renda da pesquisa: 5,5%

- Produtividade da pesquisa: 5,5%

**Qualidade da pesquisa: 30%**

- Impacto da citação: 15%

- Força da pesquisa: 5%

- Excelência da pesquisa: 5%

- Influência da pesquisa: 5%

**Indústria: 4%**

- Renda da indústria: 2%

- Patentes: 2%

**Perspectiva internacional: 7,5%**

- Proporção de alunos internacionais: 2,5%

- Proporção de equipe internacional: 2,5%

- Colaboração internacional: 2,5%

Veja o [*Times Higher Education World University Ranking 2025*](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/latest/world-ranking) completo.

*Texto original de Scott Brummitt publicado no site* [*Hotcourses Abroad*](https://www.hotcoursesabroad.com/study-abroad-info/destination-guides/times-higher-education-world-university-rankings-2025/)*. Tradução e adaptação por Brenda Bellani.*

# University of São Paulo | World University Rankings

The University of São Paulo is a large Brazilian public university, and is considered one of country's more prestigious educational institutions.

Founded in 1934, the University of São Paulo came about through a collaboration of existing schools such as the Faculdade de Direito do Largo de São Francisco (Law), the Polytechnic School (Engineering) and the Escola Superior de Agricultura Luiz de Queiroz (Agriculture).

Now, the university has created new departments, and is one of the largest institutions of higher education in Latin America.

Four of its eleven campuses can be found in the city of São Paulo while the remaining campuses are in the cities of Bauru, Lorena, Piracicaba, Pirassununga, Ribeirão Preto and two in São Carlos.

The university has an remarkable 70 libraries installed across the various campuses for students to use and enjoy.

A significant proportion of scientific papers published by Brazilian researchers are produced at the University of São Paulo.

The university also houses five affiliated hospitals, 24 museums and galleries – with half a million visitors per year – two theatres, a cinema, and its own TV channel run by students.

However, the University of São Paulo have no accommodation within campus, or outside. The search for accommodation must be carried out by students in accordance to their economic conditions and interests.

Notable alumni include Antonio Candido de Mello e Souza, a Brazilian writer, professor, sociologist and literary critic, Brazilian lawyer and Vice President Michel Miguel Elias Temer Lulia, and Guido Mantega, Brazil's former Finance Minister.

# University of Campinas | World University Rankings

## About the University of Campinas

Basic information and contact details for the University of Campinas

![institution](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/academic-ui-assets/dsc/svg/flat/institution.svg?4)

Campinas is a city in the Sao Paulo state region, and is home to the main campus of the State University of Campinas (Unicamp).

The multi-discipline university also has affiliate campuses in Brazilian cities such as Limeira and Paulínia. Campinas is known not only for its temperate climate at the Tropic of Capricorn but also its wide range of cultural centres such as dozens of cinemas and bars, known locally as “barzinhos”.

The university was opened in 1966, and although one of Brazil’s younger institutions has established itself as a primary medical and scientific research centre. As part of this research and development the university produces a high amount of patented material, outstripping other larger institutions and companies. A major breakthrough was achieved in 2003 when scientists from Unicamp licensed a patent for genetic death detection, and in more recent years scientists at Unicamp have developed a test for detection of the Zika virus.

Also in Campinas and maintaining a strong working relationship with Unicamp is the National Synchrotron Light Laboratory. This institute is a benefit to students studying physics and nanotechnology, and is home to the only particle accelerator in South America. Outside of the sciences, students at Unicamp may take undergraduate courses in arts such as Dance and Communication Studies, or in humanities such as Business Administration and Social Sciences.

International undergraduates will need to sit an exam before acceptance, which will require a strong understanding of the Portuguese language. Like all state run universities, both Brazilian and international students do not pay tuition fees. The most common airport for international students to fly into is the Guarulhos International Airport, located around 135km from the Campinas campus.

Alumni of Unicamp include actor Petrônio Gontijo, historian and gay rights activist Luiz Mott, and economist Paulo Renato Souza.

# Federal University of Rio de Janeiro | World University Rankings

The Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, sometimes known as the "University of Brazil" and commonly abbreviated to UFRJ, is one of the largest and best known universities in Brazil. Founded by the Brazilian State in 1792, the university has gone on to have an enormous influence on public life in Rio, being responsible for laboratories, libraries and hospitals.

The University operates across a number of campuses and facilities throughout Rio de Janeiro, but is primarily focused on Ilha do Fundão, an artificial island off the western shore of Rio’s famous Guanabara Bay. This campus, known as College City, offers a huge range of services and activities for students including a free shuttle bus services for crossing Rio de Janeiro, various restaurants and cafes, a sports centre, as well as accommodation for students.

UFRJ can also lay claim to a number of high-quality academic facilities, such as the largest ocean tank in the world, as well as a domestically operated maglev train system.

As one might expect for a higher education institution of this size and reach, UFRJ offers a huge range and variety of undergraduate courses (more than 170), as well and numerous avenues for postgraduate and research students. UFRJ also distinguishes itself with a significant level of international co-operation, with extensive opportunities for foreign students to come and study in Rio.

The university can also boast of having produced a succession of successful alumni, including writer Jorge Amado, Nobel Peace Prize nominee Osvaldo Aranha, and physician Oswaldo Cruz.

# Universidade Estadual Paulista (Unesp) | World University Rankings

São Paulo State University (UNESP), founded in 1976, is one of Brazil’s largest public universities with 24 campuses throughout the State of São Paulo.

Its multi-campus model allows UNESP to offer a varied academic programme with diverse activities. As one of Brazil’s foremost research universities, it cites subject strengths in health, engineering, communications, humanities, arts, social sciences and theoretical sciences.

UNESP is international recognised for the quality of its research, teaching and its initiatives to promote cultural diversity in the classroom. Its ethos emphasises critical thinking, humanist principles, sustainability, technological innovation and democratic participation in equal measures.

The university’s various campuses are also home to a diverse range of contemporary artworks, historical artefacts, farms, museums and a zoo, as well as hospitals and libraries.

São Paulo is Brazil’s wealthiest and most populous State, vibrant and cosmopolitan. Its capital, the city of São Paulo, is the country’s financial and cultural centre, home to a host of iconic architecture and events such as the São Paulo Art Biennial and the Brazilian Grand Prix. The city also hosts the largest LGBT Pride Festival in the world.

# Federal University of Minas Gerais | World University Rankings

While the first higher learning education centre in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais was created in 1839, the modern day Federal University of Minas Gerais was founded in 1927. Upon its inception UMG combined a number of schools in the area in fields of law, medicine and engineering.

More recently established courses are agronomy, performing arts, computational mathematics, and automation.

UMG is located in the east Brazilian city of Belo Horizonte, a marvel of urban planning modelled around Washington D.C. The city also has a strong footballing culture, having been a host city in the 1950 and 2014 World Cups. A key conduit for travel in and out of the city is Confins International Airport, located on the city outskirts.

Sitting below the equator, the UMG holds its winter festival every July. The celebration brings together artists from across Brazil and the world to engage in courses, workshops and street exhibitions.

Every year there is also a "Knowledge Week" on campus, with the aim of sharing information and developments across different academic branches at the university. Graduates can also sign up to Academic Enrichment activities which can help them broaden their educational horizons outside a specialised area of study.

UMG also recognises the need for the university to communicate and foster the opportunities of students across economic and ethnic backgrounds, and is committed to this goal with scholarship programmes and outreach initiatives.

Notable alumni of UMG include former Brazilian prime minister Tancredo Neves, president Dilma Rousseff, and musician Samuel Rosa. Strong connections with former students are maintained through the Always UFMG Program.

# THE World University Rankings 2022 Released

**TIMES HIGHER EDUCATION WORLD UNIVERSITY RANKINGS 2022 REVEALS PLANET’S BEST UNIVERSITIES AS UK’S UNIVERSITY OF OXFORD TOPS TABLE FOR 6TH CONSECUTIVE YEAR AND OTHERS SEE BOOST FROM COVID-19 RESEARCH**

- **UK**’s University of Oxford (1st) retains top spot for the sixth consecutive year
- A record 1,662 universities from 99 countries and regions rank, 136 more than last year
- Several universities climb table following success of Covid-19 related research
- **Mainland China** claims highest ever position in table as Tsinghua University and Peking University tie in 16th and sees record number of universities in the top 200 (10)
- **US** (8) and **UK** (2) dominate overall top 10 for the second year in a row
- **Japan**, **South Korea**, **Russia**, **Singapore**, and **Hong Kong** all achieve highest positions since the new methodology was introduced in 2016
- **Hong Kong** records its highest ever number of universities in the top 100 (4)
- Latin America and Caribbean region see record participating universities (125)
- 175 universities make their debuts in the 2022 ranking, **France’s** recent merger university Institut Polytechnique de Paris (95th) is the highest-ranking debutant
- **Palestine** enters rankings for first time in world’s top 500 and is one of five new countries and territories making their debut alongside **Azerbaijan**, **Ecuador**, **Ethiopia** and **Fiji**

- **View the full THE World University Rankings 2022:** <https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/2022/world-ranking>
- **View the full THE World University Rankings 2022 methodology:** <https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/world-university-rankings-2022-methodology>

**2 September 2021**

Times Higher Education (THE) has today announced the results of the THE World University Rankings 2022 with the **UK’s** University of Oxford – which led the way in the global search for a Covid-19 vaccine – retaining top spot for an impressive sixth consecutive year. This is despite a record 1,662 universities from 99 countries and regions appearing in the table. **Azerbaijan**, **Ecuador**, **Ethiopia**, **Fiji** and **Palestine are** all represented for the first time, and include an analysis of 108 million citations to 14.4 million research publications, as well as a survey of over 22,000 academics

**Top Ten Universities Hold On For Fourth Year**

The top 10 positions are all held by the same universities for a second consecutive year, though only three appear in the same ranking position as last year. California Institute of Technology (=2nd), and Harvard University (=2nd) in the **US** both move up, while the **UK**’s University of Cambridge (=5th) climbs back into the top 5 after dropping to 6th last year. Princeton University in the **US** (7th) also improves, moving up two places.

**Below Table: Overall Top 10**

| **University Name** | **Country / Region** | **2022 Rank** | **2021 Rank** | **Change** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| University of Oxford | United Kingdom | 1 | 1 | – |
| California Institute of Technology | United States | =2 | 4 | + 2 |
| Harvard University | United States | =2 | 3 | + 1 |
| Stanford University | United States | 4 | 2 | – 2 |
| University of Cambridge | United Kingdom | =5 | 6 | + 1 |
| Massachusetts Institute of Technology | United States | =5 | 5 | – |
| Princeton University | United States | 7 | 9 | + 2 |
| University of California, Berkeley | United States | 8 | 7 | – 1 |
| Yale University | United States | 9 | 8 | – 1 |
| The University of Chicago | United States | 10 | 10 | – |

**Universities See Boost From Covid-19 Research**

In a year dominated by the ongoing Covid-19 pandemic, the rankings reflect the vital role of universities in understanding and managing the crisis as a number of institutions see significant boosts in their citation scores (which examine university’s research influence, and look at their role in spreading new knowledge and ideas) from Covid-19 focused research.

A number of medical universities moved up the table since last year following Covid-19 research. To name a few, **Mainland China’s** Capital Medical University (501-600), **Taiwan’s** Asia University, Taiwan (501-600), **Saudi Arabia’s** Umm Al-Qura University (601-800), and **Estonia’s** Tallinn University of Technology (601-800), all moved up at least one ranking band as a result.

**Mainland China Continues Rapid Rise**

**Mainland China** enjoys some striking success stories as it continues its rise up the table, with Peking University and Tsinghua University (=16th) claiming **mainland China’s** highest ever finish, and giving it two top 20 places for the first time ever. There are also a record number of **mainland Chinese** universities ranked in the top 200 (10) as Wuhan University (157th), Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech) (=162nd), and Huazhong University of Science and Technology (181th) all move into the band.

**The top 200 – Record Highs and New Entrants**

This year, **Japan, South Korea, Russia, Singapore,** and **Hong Kong** all claim their best ever finishes since the current methodology was introduced in 2016 as **Japan’s** University of Tokyo (=35th), **Hong Kong**’s University of Hong Kong (=30th), **South Korea**’s Seoul National University (=54th), **Singapore**’s National University of Singapore (21st), and **Russia**’s Lomonosov Moscow State University (=158th) all climb the table.

The top 200 also sees eight new entrants as universities from mainland China, Germany, Saudi Arabia, Austria, France and Italy all move into the band.

**Below Table: New Entrants into Top 200**

**Debutants and Best Represented Countries and Regions**

**France’s** Institut Polytechnique de Paris (95th) is the highest ranked of 175 debutant universities this year (following its recent merger), and the only one to rank in the top 100, closely followed by another **French** university (and recent merger, formerly 'University Paris-Saclay’), Université Paris-Saclay (=117th). No other university debuts in the top 200.

The highest number of new entrants are from the **US** (14), helping it achieve a record number of ranked institutions as a result (183). Following close behind are **Iran** and **Russia** both with 12 new entrants, **Turkey** (11), **Brazil** and **India** (both 9).

Once again, the **US** is the most represented country or region in the ranking (183 universities). They are followed by **Japan** (118), **UK** (101), **mainland China** (97), and India (71). **Fiji**, **Azerbaijan**, **Ecuador**, **Ethiopia**, and **Palestine** are all represented for the first time. **Phil Baty, Chief Knowledge Officer, THE, commented:**

“*The world’s elite universities have enjoyed a long period of dominance at the top of the table with help from historic repuatation, global status, and reliable income. But our data shows us that there are clear shifts happening across higher education around the world. We are already seeing clear disruption to the established norms from mainland China, and record highs for Japan, South Korea, Singapore, and Hong Kong show that Asia is continuing to benefit from the focus and investment in higher education across the continent.*

*In the coming years it will be interesting to see whether the US, UK and other world-leading higher education systems can respond to the challenges of Covid-19, including attracting international academic and student talent, and a possibly serious impact on already stretched funding, to hold onto their positions at the very top of the table.”*

# Study in Brazil

Perhaps best-known for its sport and breathtaking scenery, Brazil is home to more than 2,500 universities, with elite institutions including the University of São Paulo, the biggest public university in the country and one of the best in Latin America. Also home to São Paulo State University, Brazil’s largest city and financial capital is also considered the nation’s cultural centre, home to a plethora of museums, art galleries and concert halls - and it has a vibrant nightlife.

Brazil’s 8,000km of coastline include thousands of spectacular beaches. Also unmissable is carnival season, which starts in February. Rio de Janeiro’s carnival is the biggest in the world, with more than two million people lining the streets each day to witness more than 300 bands and samba schools.

Brazil produces a third of the world’s coffee and is renowned for a wide variety of street food. The country's football team has won the World Cup more than any other nation, and football, by far the most popular sport, has been likened to a religion in the country. But many also like volleyball and, to a slightly lesser extent, mixed martial arts and basketball. Famous Brazilians include footballer Pelé and the late Formula 1 racing driver Ayrton Senna.

Public universities have free tuition for home and international students, but places are limited and most students attend private institutions.

# University of São Paulo | World University Rankings

The University of São Paulo is a large Brazilian public university, and is considered one of country's more prestigious educational institutions.

Founded in 1934, the University of São Paulo came about through a collaboration of existing schools such as the Faculdade de Direito do Largo de São Francisco (Law), the Polytechnic School (Engineering) and the Escola Superior de Agricultura Luiz de Queiroz (Agriculture).

Now, the university has created new departments, and is one of the largest institutions of higher education in Latin America.

Four of its eleven campuses can be found in the city of São Paulo while the remaining campuses are in the cities of Bauru, Lorena, Piracicaba, Pirassununga, Ribeirão Preto and two in São Carlos.

The university has an remarkable 70 libraries installed across the various campuses for students to use and enjoy.

A significant proportion of scientific papers published by Brazilian researchers are produced at the University of São Paulo.

The university also houses five affiliated hospitals, 24 museums and galleries – with half a million visitors per year – two theatres, a cinema, and its own TV channel run by students.

However, the University of São Paulo have no accommodation within campus, or outside. The search for accommodation must be carried out by students in accordance to their economic conditions and interests.

Notable alumni include Antonio Candido de Mello e Souza, a Brazilian writer, professor, sociologist and literary critic, Brazilian lawyer and Vice President Michel Miguel Elias Temer Lulia, and Guido Mantega, Brazil's former Finance Minister.

## About the University of Campinas

Basic information and contact details for the University of Campinas

![institution](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/academic-ui-assets/dsc/svg/flat/institution.svg?4)

Campinas is a city in the Sao Paulo state region, and is home to the main campus of the State University of Campinas (Unicamp).

The multi-discipline university also has affiliate campuses in Brazilian cities such as Limeira and Paulínia. Campinas is known not only for its temperate climate at the Tropic of Capricorn but also its wide range of cultural centres such as dozens of cinemas and bars, known locally as “barzinhos”.

The university was opened in 1966, and although one of Brazil’s younger institutions has established itself as a primary medical and scientific research centre. As part of this research and development the university produces a high amount of patented material, outstripping other larger institutions and companies. A major breakthrough was achieved in 2003 when scientists from Unicamp licensed a patent for genetic death detection, and in more recent years scientists at Unicamp have developed a test for detection of the Zika virus.

Also in Campinas and maintaining a strong working relationship with Unicamp is the National Synchrotron Light Laboratory. This institute is a benefit to students studying physics and nanotechnology, and is home to the only particle accelerator in South America. Outside of the sciences, students at Unicamp may take undergraduate courses in arts such as Dance and Communication Studies, or in humanities such as Business Administration and Social Sciences.

International undergraduates will need to sit an exam before acceptance, which will require a strong understanding of the Portuguese language. Like all state run universities, both Brazilian and international students do not pay tuition fees. The most common airport for international students to fly into is the Guarulhos International Airport, located around 135km from the Campinas campus.

Alumni of Unicamp include actor Petrônio Gontijo, historian and gay rights activist Luiz Mott, and economist Paulo Renato Souza.

# Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025

![Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025](https://images-intl.prod.aws.idp-connect.com/hca-cont/img/default/img_px.gif)

O aguardado *Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025* acaba de ser divulgado com as melhores universidades do mundo. Após analisar minuciosamente 2.092 instituições de 115 países e regiões, o ranking proporciona um panorama completo sobre o ensino superior global. Confira os destaques da nova edição!

## **Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025**

A [University of Oxford](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study-in-the-uk/applying-to-university/como-se-candidatar-a-oxford-no-reino-unido/) é a melhor universidade do mundo pelo nono ano consecutivo, de acordo com a Times Higher Education. Da mesma forma que no ano passado, todas as instituições nas dez primeiras posições são do Reino Unido e dos Estados Unidos. Não só isso, as universidades em questão também são exatamente as mesmas, algumas apenas trocaram de lugar. A [Princeton University](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study-in-usa/city-focus/como-estudar-na-universidade-de-princeton-estados-unidos/) subiu duas posições para o quarto lugar, enquanto a [Stanford University](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study-in-usa/city-focus/como-se-candidatar-a-stanford-university/) caiu quatro posições para o sexto.

Outros países começam a aparecer a partir do 11º lugar, ocupado pela [ETH Zurich da Suíça](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study-in-switzerland/city-focus/eth-zurique-na-suica/), seguida por duas universidades da China. A Tsinghua University e a University of Peking subiram uma posição em relação ao ano passado. A primeira, inclusive, liderou recentemente o [*Times Higher Education Asia University Rankings*](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study-in-china/city-focus/melhores-universidades-da-asia-2024/)das melhores universidades da Ásia.

### **As melhores universidades do mundo segundo Times Higher Education 2025**

1. University of Oxford, Reino Unido

2. Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), EUA

3. Harvard University, EUA

4. Princeton University, EUA

5. University of Cambridge, Reino Unido

6. Stanford University, EUA

7. California Institute of Technology, EUA

8. University of California, Berkeley, EUA

9. Imperial College London, Reino Unido

10. Yale University, EUA

[![Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025](https://images-intl.prod.aws.idp-connect.com/hca-cont/img/default/img_px.gif)](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study/international/schools-colleges-university/list.html) 

Como de costume, as [universidades dos Estados Unidos](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study/us-usa/international/schools-colleges-university/211/list.html) têm o melhor desempenho geral. A maioria das 30 melhores do mundo são estadunidenses, incluindo o segundo lugar, o [MIT](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study-in-usa/city-focus/por-que-o-mit-e-uma-das-melhores-universidades-do-mundo/), agora classificado como a melhor instituição na América, tomando a posição antes ocupada pela Stanford. O Reino Unido também continua bem com 12 instituições entre as 100 melhores.

A edição não foi muito positiva para as universidades da Austrália e Nova Zelândia. Dezessete das instituições australianas caíram na lista e apenas quatro subiram de posição, entre elas, a [UNSW Sydney](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study/australia/school-college-university/unsw-sydney-university-of-new-south-wales/72233/international.html) e a [Macquarie University](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study/australia/school-college-university/macquarie-university/72221/international.html). Nenhuma das oito universidades da Nova Zelândia melhorou sua posição em relação à edição 2024. No entanto, ambos os países mostram sua força geral, com um total combinado de 12 instituições dentro do top 250. A melhor de todas é a [University of Melbourne](https://www.hotcourses.com.br/study/australia/school-college-university/the-university-of-melbourne/879/international.html), em 39º lugar.

Já a Ásia continua a progredir a cada edição. A região tem uma incomparável aparição de 853 universidades no *Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025* - 116 a mais do que no ano passado. Embora a maioria seja da China, incluindo sete no top 100, quase todo o continente conseguiu um lugar na lista. A Nanyang Technological University, de Singapura, por exemplo, subiu duas posições e ficou entre as 30 melhores do mundo, juntamente à sua conterrânea National University of Singapore, em 17a. E a japonesa University of Tokyo ficou em 28a.

Confira o top 30 do *Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025*:

11. ETH Zurich, Suíça

12. Tsinghua University

13. Peking University

=14. University of Chicago

=14. University of Pennsylvania

16. Johns Hopkins University

17. National University of Singapore

=18. Columbia University

=18. University of California, Los Angeles

20. Cornell University

21. University of Toronto

=22. UCL (University College London)

=22. University of Michigan-Ann Arbor

24. Carnegie Mellon University

25. University of Washington

26. Technical University of Munich

27. Duke University

28. University of Tokyo

29. University of Edinburgh

30. Nanyang Technological University

### **USP fica entre as 200 melhores do mundo**

O Brasil é um dos três países que conseguiram um lugar entre as 200 melhores universidades do mundo em relação a 2024, com a Arábia Saudita e os Emirados Árabes Unidos, no *Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025*, "destacando a ascensão do ensino superior em mercados emergentes", segundo o site oficial do ranking.

A Universidade de São Paulo (USP) ficou na 199a posição, seu melhor desempenho desde 2013, graças, principalmente, à melhoria no indicativo relacionado à indústria (renda e patentes).

A Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio de Janeiro (PUC-Rio), a terceira instituição brasileira mais bem classificada, também melhorou sua posição, subindo da faixa 801-1.000 para 601-800 este ano. As outras três no top cinco do Brasil permaneceram nas mesmas faixas: a Universidade Estadual de Campinas (Unicamp) em 351-400; e a Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ) e a Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS), ambas em 601-800.

O Brasil agora tem 61 universidades classificadas no *Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025*, com cinco instituições a mais este ano. Em comparação ao resto da América do Sul, as universidades brasileiras têm a maior pontuação média nos pilares de ensino, ambiente de pesquisa e indústria.

#### **A metodologia do Times Higher Education World University Ranking**

O *Times Higher Education World University Ranking 2025* baseia-se no desempenho das universidades em cinco áreas diferentes - ensino, ambiente de pesquisa, qualidade da pesquisa, indústria e perspectiva internacional -, medidas e pontuadas de acordo com 18 indicadores de desempenho, todos com ponderação porcentual. Quando combinados, eles formam uma pontuação geral para cada universidade na lista.

**Ensino: 29,5%**

- Reputação do ensino: 15%

- Proporção entre funcionários e alunos: 4,5%

- Proporção de doutorado para bacharelado: 2%

- Proporção de professores com título de doutor: 5,5%

- Renda institucional: 2,5%

**Ambiente de pesquisa: 29%**

- Reputação da pesquisa: 18%

- Renda da pesquisa: 5,5%

- Produtividade da pesquisa: 5,5%

**Qualidade da pesquisa: 30%**

- Impacto da citação: 15%

- Força da pesquisa: 5%

- Excelência da pesquisa: 5%

- Influência da pesquisa: 5%

**Indústria: 4%**

- Renda da indústria: 2%

- Patentes: 2%

**Perspectiva internacional: 7,5%**

- Proporção de alunos internacionais: 2,5%

- Proporção de equipe internacional: 2,5%

- Colaboração internacional: 2,5%

Veja o [*Times Higher Education World University Ranking 2025*](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/latest/world-ranking) completo.

*Texto original de Scott Brummitt publicado no site* [*Hotcourses Abroad*](https://www.hotcoursesabroad.com/study-abroad-info/destination-guides/times-higher-education-world-university-rankings-2025/)*. Tradução e adaptação por Brenda Bellani.*

# University of São Paulo | World University Rankings

The University of São Paulo is a large Brazilian public university, and is considered one of country's more prestigious educational institutions.

Founded in 1934, the University of São Paulo came about through a collaboration of existing schools such as the Faculdade de Direito do Largo de São Francisco (Law), the Polytechnic School (Engineering) and the Escola Superior de Agricultura Luiz de Queiroz (Agriculture).

Now, the university has created new departments, and is one of the largest institutions of higher education in Latin America.

Four of its eleven campuses can be found in the city of São Paulo while the remaining campuses are in the cities of Bauru, Lorena, Piracicaba, Pirassununga, Ribeirão Preto and two in São Carlos.

The university has an remarkable 70 libraries installed across the various campuses for students to use and enjoy.

A significant proportion of scientific papers published by Brazilian researchers are produced at the University of São Paulo.

The university also houses five affiliated hospitals, 24 museums and galleries – with half a million visitors per year – two theatres, a cinema, and its own TV channel run by students.

However, the University of São Paulo have no accommodation within campus, or outside. The search for accommodation must be carried out by students in accordance to their economic conditions and interests.

Notable alumni include Antonio Candido de Mello e Souza, a Brazilian writer, professor, sociologist and literary critic, Brazilian lawyer and Vice President Michel Miguel Elias Temer Lulia, and Guido Mantega, Brazil's former Finance Minister.

![institution](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/academic-ui-assets/dsc/svg/flat/institution.svg?4)

Campinas is a city in the Sao Paulo state region, and is home to the main campus of the State University of Campinas (Unicamp).

The multi-discipline university also has affiliate campuses in Brazilian cities such as Limeira and Paulínia. Campinas is known not only for its temperate climate at the Tropic of Capricorn but also its wide range of cultural centres such as dozens of cinemas and bars, known locally as “barzinhos”.

The university was opened in 1966, and although one of Brazil’s younger institutions has established itself as a primary medical and scientific research centre. As part of this research and development the university produces a high amount of patented material, outstripping other larger institutions and companies. A major breakthrough was achieved in 2003 when scientists from Unicamp licensed a patent for genetic death detection, and in more recent years scientists at Unicamp have developed a test for detection of the Zika virus.

Also in Campinas and maintaining a strong working relationship with Unicamp is the National Synchrotron Light Laboratory. This institute is a benefit to students studying physics and nanotechnology, and is home to the only particle accelerator in South America. Outside of the sciences, students at Unicamp may take undergraduate courses in arts such as Dance and Communication Studies, or in humanities such as Business Administration and Social Sciences.

International undergraduates will need to sit an exam before acceptance, which will require a strong understanding of the Portuguese language. Like all state run universities, both Brazilian and international students do not pay tuition fees. The most common airport for international students to fly into is the Guarulhos International Airport, located around 135km from the Campinas campus.

Alumni of Unicamp include actor Petrônio Gontijo, historian and gay rights activist Luiz Mott, and economist Paulo Renato Souza.

# Federal University of Rio de Janeiro | World University Rankings

The Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, sometimes known as the "University of Brazil" and commonly abbreviated to UFRJ, is one of the largest and best known universities in Brazil. Founded by the Brazilian State in 1792, the university has gone on to have an enormous influence on public life in Rio, being responsible for laboratories, libraries and hospitals.

The University operates across a number of campuses and facilities throughout Rio de Janeiro, but is primarily focused on Ilha do Fundão, an artificial island off the western shore of Rio’s famous Guanabara Bay. This campus, known as College City, offers a huge range of services and activities for students including a free shuttle bus services for crossing Rio de Janeiro, various restaurants and cafes, a sports centre, as well as accommodation for students.

UFRJ can also lay claim to a number of high-quality academic facilities, such as the largest ocean tank in the world, as well as a domestically operated maglev train system.

As one might expect for a higher education institution of this size and reach, UFRJ offers a huge range and variety of undergraduate courses (more than 170), as well and numerous avenues for postgraduate and research students. UFRJ also distinguishes itself with a significant level of international co-operation, with extensive opportunities for foreign students to come and study in Rio.

The university can also boast of having produced a succession of successful alumni, including writer Jorge Amado, Nobel Peace Prize nominee Osvaldo Aranha, and physician Oswaldo Cruz.

# Universidade Estadual Paulista (Unesp) | World University Rankings

São Paulo State University (UNESP), founded in 1976, is one of Brazil’s largest public universities with 24 campuses throughout the State of São Paulo.

Its multi-campus model allows UNESP to offer a varied academic programme with diverse activities. As one of Brazil’s foremost research universities, it cites subject strengths in health, engineering, communications, humanities, arts, social sciences and theoretical sciences.

UNESP is international recognised for the quality of its research, teaching and its initiatives to promote cultural diversity in the classroom. Its ethos emphasises critical thinking, humanist principles, sustainability, technological innovation and democratic participation in equal measures.

The university’s various campuses are also home to a diverse range of contemporary artworks, historical artefacts, farms, museums and a zoo, as well as hospitals and libraries.

São Paulo is Brazil’s wealthiest and most populous State, vibrant and cosmopolitan. Its capital, the city of São Paulo, is the country’s financial and cultural centre, home to a host of iconic architecture and events such as the São Paulo Art Biennial and the Brazilian Grand Prix. The city also hosts the largest LGBT Pride Festival in the world.

# Federal University of Minas Gerais | World University Rankings

While the first higher learning education centre in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais was created in 1839, the modern day Federal University of Minas Gerais was founded in 1927. Upon its inception UMG combined a number of schools in the area in fields of law, medicine and engineering.

More recently established courses are agronomy, performing arts, computational mathematics, and automation.

UMG is located in the east Brazilian city of Belo Horizonte, a marvel of urban planning modelled around Washington D.C. The city also has a strong footballing culture, having been a host city in the 1950 and 2014 World Cups. A key conduit for travel in and out of the city is Confins International Airport, located on the city outskirts.

Sitting below the equator, the UMG holds its winter festival every July. The celebration brings together artists from across Brazil and the world to engage in courses, workshops and street exhibitions.

Every year there is also a "Knowledge Week" on campus, with the aim of sharing information and developments across different academic branches at the university. Graduates can also sign up to Academic Enrichment activities which can help them broaden their educational horizons outside a specialised area of study.

UMG also recognises the need for the university to communicate and foster the opportunities of students across economic and ethnic backgrounds, and is committed to this goal with scholarship programmes and outreach initiatives.

Notable alumni of UMG include former Brazilian prime minister Tancredo Neves, president Dilma Rousseff, and musician Samuel Rosa. Strong connections with former students are maintained through the Always UFMG Program.

# THE World University Rankings 2022 Released

**TIMES HIGHER EDUCATION WORLD UNIVERSITY RANKINGS 2022 REVEALS PLANET’S BEST UNIVERSITIES AS UK’S UNIVERSITY OF OXFORD TOPS TABLE FOR 6TH CONSECUTIVE YEAR AND OTHERS SEE BOOST FROM COVID-19 RESEARCH**

- **UK**’s University of Oxford (1st) retains top spot for the sixth consecutive year
- A record 1,662 universities from 99 countries and regions rank, 136 more than last year
- Several universities climb table following success of Covid-19 related research
- **Mainland China** claims highest ever position in table as Tsinghua University and Peking University tie in 16th and sees record number of universities in the top 200 (10)
- **US** (8) and **UK** (2) dominate overall top 10 for the second year in a row
- **Japan**, **South Korea**, **Russia**, **Singapore**, and **Hong Kong** all achieve highest positions since the new methodology was introduced in 2016
- **Hong Kong** records its highest ever number of universities in the top 100 (4)
- Latin America and Caribbean region see record participating universities (125)
- 175 universities make their debuts in the 2022 ranking, **France’s** recent merger university Institut Polytechnique de Paris (95th) is the highest-ranking debutant
- **Palestine** enters rankings for first time in world’s top 500 and is one of five new countries and territories making their debut alongside **Azerbaijan**, **Ecuador**, **Ethiopia** and **Fiji**

- **View the full THE World University Rankings 2022:** <https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/2022/world-ranking>
- **View the full THE World University Rankings 2022 methodology:** <https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/world-university-rankings-2022-methodology>

**2 September 2021**

Times Higher Education (THE) has today announced the results of the THE World University Rankings 2022 with the **UK’s** University of Oxford – which led the way in the global search for a Covid-19 vaccine – retaining top spot for an impressive sixth consecutive year. This is despite a record 1,662 universities from 99 countries and regions appearing in the table. **Azerbaijan**, **Ecuador**, **Ethiopia**, **Fiji** and **Palestine are** all represented for the first time, and include an analysis of 108 million citations to 14.4 million research publications, as well as a survey of over 22,000 academics

**Top Ten Universities Hold On For Fourth Year**

The top 10 positions are all held by the same universities for a second consecutive year, though only three appear in the same ranking position as last year. California Institute of Technology (=2nd), and Harvard University (=2nd) in the **US** both move up, while the **UK**’s University of Cambridge (=5th) climbs back into the top 5 after dropping to 6th last year. Princeton University in the **US** (7th) also improves, moving up two places.

**Below Table: Overall Top 10**

| The University of Chicago | United States | 10 | 10 | – |

**Universities See Boost From Covid-19 Research**

In a year dominated by the ongoing Covid-19 pandemic, the rankings reflect the vital role of universities in understanding and managing the crisis as a number of institutions see significant boosts in their citation scores (which examine university’s research influence, and look at their role in spreading new knowledge and ideas) from Covid-19 focused research.

A number of medical universities moved up the table since last year following Covid-19 research. To name a few, **Mainland China’s** Capital Medical University (501-600), **Taiwan’s** Asia University, Taiwan (501-600), **Saudi Arabia’s** Umm Al-Qura University (601-800), and **Estonia’s** Tallinn University of Technology (601-800), all moved up at least one ranking band as a result.

**Mainland China Continues Rapid Rise**

**Mainland China** enjoys some striking success stories as it continues its rise up the table, with Peking University and Tsinghua University (=16th) claiming **mainland China’s** highest ever finish, and giving it two top 20 places for the first time ever. There are also a record number of **mainland Chinese** universities ranked in the top 200 (10) as Wuhan University (157th), Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech) (=162nd), and Huazhong University of Science and Technology (181th) all move into the band.

**The top 200 – Record Highs and New Entrants**

This year, **Japan, South Korea, Russia, Singapore,** and **Hong Kong** all claim their best ever finishes since the current methodology was introduced in 2016 as **Japan’s** University of Tokyo (=35th), **Hong Kong**’s University of Hong Kong (=30th), **South Korea**’s Seoul National University (=54th), **Singapore**’s National University of Singapore (21st), and **Russia**’s Lomonosov Moscow State University (=158th) all climb the table.

The top 200 also sees eight new entrants as universities from mainland China, Germany, Saudi Arabia, Austria, France and Italy all move into the band.

**Phil Baty, Chief Knowledge Officer, THE, commented:**

“*The world’s elite universities have enjoyed a long period of dominance at the top of the table with help from historic repuatation, global status, and reliable income. But our data shows us that there are clear shifts happening across higher education around the world. We are already seeing clear disruption to the established norms from mainland China, and record highs for Japan, South Korea, Singapore, and Hong Kong show that Asia is continuing to benefit from the focus and investment in higher education across the continent.*

# Study in Brazil

Perhaps best-known for its sport and breathtaking scenery, Brazil is home to more than 2,500 universities, with elite institutions including the University of São Paulo, the biggest public university in the country and one of the best in Latin America. Also home to São Paulo State University, Brazil’s largest city and financial capital is also considered the nation’s cultural centre, home to a plethora of museums, art galleries and concert halls - and it has a vibrant nightlife.

Brazil’s 8,000km of coastline include thousands of spectacular beaches. Also unmissable is carnival season, which starts in February. Rio de Janeiro’s carnival is the biggest in the world, with more than two million people lining the streets each day to witness more than 300 bands and samba schools.

Brazil produces a third of the world’s coffee and is renowned for a wide variety of street food. The country's football team has won the World Cup more than any other nation, and football, by far the most popular sport, has been likened to a religion in the country. But many also like volleyball and, to a slightly lesser extent, mixed martial arts and basketball. Famous Brazilians include footballer Pelé and the late Formula 1 racing driver Ayrton Senna.

Public universities have free tuition for home and international students, but places are limited and most students attend private institutions.

# University of São Paulo | World University Rankings

The University of São Paulo is a large Brazilian public university, and is considered one of country's more prestigious educational institutions.

Founded in 1934, the University of São Paulo came about through a collaboration of existing schools such as the Faculdade de Direito do Largo de São Francisco (Law), the Polytechnic School (Engineering) and the Escola Superior de Agricultura Luiz de Queiroz (Agriculture).

Now, the university has created new departments, and is one of the largest institutions of higher education in Latin America.

Four of its eleven campuses can be found in the city of São Paulo while the remaining campuses are in the cities of Bauru, Lorena, Piracicaba, Pirassununga, Ribeirão Preto and two in São Carlos.

The university has an remarkable 70 libraries installed across the various campuses for students to use and enjoy.

A significant proportion of scientific papers published by Brazilian researchers are produced at the University of São Paulo.

The university also houses five affiliated hospitals, 24 museums and galleries – with half a million visitors per year – two theatres, a cinema, and its own TV channel run by students.

However, the University of São Paulo have no accommodation within campus, or outside. The search for accommodation must be carried out by students in accordance to their economic conditions and interests.

Notable alumni include Antonio Candido de Mello e Souza, a Brazilian writer, professor, sociologist and literary critic, Brazilian lawyer and Vice President Michel Miguel Elias Temer Lulia, and Guido Mantega, Brazil's former Finance Minister.
